design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated (1:1) to resection with or without elective neck dissection using a central computer minimisation program.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated using a central minimisation system with adequate allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Allocation concealment was achieved using a central randomisation system. Patients were randomised (1:1 allocation) after research nurses telephoned Saving Faces, the trial co-ordinating centre. A minimisation computer program stratified patients by age (<40, 40–64, 65+years), tumour stage (T1 and T2) and surgeon.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of surgical intervention was not possible, an intention-to-treat analysis was performed, and there is no indication that deviations beyond crossover affected trial conduct inappropriately.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In those randomised to have resection only, seven patients actually had a neck dissection as well and for another patient what they had was unreported. In those allocated to END, 12 had resection only... Primary analyses were by intention-to-treat (ITT).

domain_judgments.rationale: Virtually complete follow-up data were available for time-to-event outcomes across the randomized cohort with 250 evaluable patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two hundred fifty-five patients agreed to be randomised and they came from 25 hospitals (18 June 2007 to 10 July 2015), and were operated on by 52 surgeons; five patients were found to be ineligible and so excluded from all analyses. Median follow-up was 57 months (25–75th centile 43–61 months). Similar numbers of patients in both trial groups attended each assessment visit.

domain_judgments.rationale: Overall survival is an objective endpoint that cannot be influenced by lack of blinding, and secondary recurrence endpoints were verified according to standard pathological and radiological diagnostic criteria across both groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was overall survival (OS; death from any cause, and those who did not die were censored when last known to be alive). Secondary outcomes included: disease-free survival...

domain_judgments.rationale: The study followed a registered trial protocol (UKCRN 2069, NCT00571883) with prespecified primary and secondary outcomes analysed using standard ITT statistical methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary analyses were by intention-to-treat (ITT). Prespecified per-protocol analyses were performed for patients who had the randomised surgical procedure... Time-to-event outcomes were analysed using Cox regression (hazard ratio, HR), after confirming the assumption of proportional hazards.

overall_summary: The randomized trial had robust central allocation concealment, low missing outcome data, prespecified intention-to-treat analyses, and objective primary endpoints (overall survival and disease-free survival), resulting in a low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: The study is described as a multicenter prospective randomized trial where patients were stratified by T classification and allocated to elective neck dissection or observation using sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although sealed envelopes stratified by T classification were used, there is no mention of sequence generation methods or whether envelopes were sequentially numbered and opaque, raising some concerns regarding allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two sets of sealed envelopes, 1 set for T1 patients and another set for T2 patients, were used for the randomization of patients to either observation or elective neck dissection.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was not feasible given the nature of the surgical intervention vs observation, and one post-randomization exclusion occurred because of a post-hoc pathological finding rather than strict intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One clinically T2 patient who was randomized to the observation arm was found to have pathologic T3 and therefore was excluded.

domain_judgments.rationale: Apart from one patient excluded post-randomization, outcome data for nodal recurrence and mortality were complete for all remaining 71 randomized participants over long follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the other 53 patients who were still alive, none of them had tumor at the last follow-up; the minimum follow-up duration of these 53 patients was 34 months (mean, 86 months; longest, 122 months).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary endpoints (mortality and disease-specific survival) are objective outcomes unlikely to be influenced by lack of blinding of outcome assessors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The main outcome assessment parameter was node-related mortality. It was defined as the percentage of patients who died of nodal metastasis not associated with local or distant metastasis. The secondary outcome assessment parameter was the 5-year tumor-specific survival rate.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered in a clinical trial registry and reported outcomes align with the pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The research protocol was posted to the website of clinical trial public information center ofThe University ofHong Kong for public access of information in 2005 (http:// www.hkclinicaltrials.com, clinical trial registration number HKCTR-17, registration name: prospective randomized study of selective I, II, III neck dissection for stage I and II squamous cell carcinoma of oral tongue).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to potential issues in allocation sequence generation/concealment (unspecified details on envelope sealing and generation) and a post-randomization exclusion.

design_rationale: Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to elective or therapeutic neck dissection using a prepared computerized block design.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was generated via a prepared computerized block design with pre-stratification, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly assigned to undergo either elective or therapeutic neck dissection in a 1:1 ratio with the use of a prepared computerized block design. Patients were stratified according to tumor site... tumor stage... sex, and findings on neck ultrasonography... before randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Surgical trials cannot be blinded, but non-adherence was very low and analyses were conducted according to the intention-to-treat principle.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary and secondary end points were assessed in the intention-to-treat population and tested by means of two-sided log-rank tests.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was low, balanced across trial arms, and appropriately addressed with survival analysis censoring.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The numbers of patients who were lost to follow-up were similar in the two groups (25 of 243 patients [10.3%] in elective-surgery group and 22 of 253 patients [8.7%] in the therapeutic-surgery group).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of overall survival (all-cause mortality) is objective and immune to detection or assessor bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was overall survival, which was defined as the interval between the date of randomization and the date of death from any cause.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were analyzed according to a prespecified protocol with predefined interim stopping boundaries monitored by an independent data and safety monitoring committee.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This single-center trial was initiated after approval from the institutional ethics committee and was monitored by the institutional data and safety monitoring committee. The study protocol and amendments are available with the full text of this article at NEJM.org.

overall_summary: The trial was a well-conducted randomized controlled trial with robust computer-generated allocation, minimal loss to follow-up, intention-to-treat analysis, and an objective primary mortality endpoint pre-specified in the protocol.

design_rationale: The authors explicitly state that this was a prospective, randomized study in which patients stratified by stage were randomized to receive resection alone or resection plus elective supraomohyoid neck dissection.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although patients were stated to be stratified and randomized, the specific method of sequence generation and allocation concealment was not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All 67 patients were stratified by stage, T1, N0; and T2, N0; and those in each stage were randomized to receive 1 of 2 types of treatment: resection alone (RA) or resection plus elective supraomohyoid neck dissection (RSOND).

domain_judgments.rationale: Surgical interventions were delivered as assigned, and analysis included all allocated patients according to an intention-to-treat approach without evidence of non-protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirty-three (49%) patients were treated with RA... Thirty-four (51%) patients in the RSOND group had dissection of levels 1, 2, and 3, plus resection of submandibular gland...

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for treatment failures, recurrences, and disease-free/overall survival appear complete for all 67 randomized patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analysis of Treatment Failures in 67 Patients With T1 and T2 NO Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Oral Cavity... Figure. Impact of types of treatment... on disease-free survival in 67 patients

domain_judgments.rationale: Recurrence and survival are objective clinical and histopathological outcomes unlikely to be biased by lack of blinding of outcome assessors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients had the primary lesion and cervical lymph nodes examined by microscopic analysis of frozen sections.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial protocol or prospective statistical analysis plan was cited or available to rule out selective reporting of outcomes and subgroup analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The Mantel-Haenszel chi-square method was used to analyze the proportion of failures and the association power of certain variables with types of treatment. The impact of the two modalities of treatment on disease-free and overall survival was assessed by the Kaplan-Meier actuarial method and Wilcoxon's signed rank test.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to insufficient details regarding the random sequence generation and allocation concealment methods, as well as the lack of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified analysis plan.

design_rationale: Participants with T1-2 N0M0 oral tongue cancer were explicitly stated to be randomized using previously generated random numbers to either hemiglossectomy alone or hemiglossectomy plus ipsilateral radical neck dissection.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random numbers were used to generate the sequence, but there is no information provided regarding allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All T1-2 N0M0 patients, staged according to the criteria of American Joint Committee [3], with histologically proven squamous cell carcinoma of oral tongue were randomized from previously generated random numbers to either hemiglossectomy alone (group A) or hemiglossectomy and ipsilateral radical neck dissection (group B).

domain_judgments.rationale: Fourteen randomized patients (12 did not take treatment, 2 unfit) were excluded from initial treatment analysis, and analysis was further restricted to only 35 patients who completed 1 year of follow-up, violating intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 73 patients have been entered into the protocol to date. Twelve patients did not take treatment after entry and two patients were declared unfit for surgery. Thus, 59 patients have completed initial treatment. Thirty-five of these patients who have completed a minimum of 1 year of follow-up after completion of treatment have been analysed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Out of 73 enrolled/randomized patients, only 35 (less than 50%) were included in the reported analysis, presenting substantial missing outcome data without demonstration that missingness was unrelated to outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 73 patients have been entered into the protocol to date. Twelve patients did not take treatment after entry and two patients were declared unfit for surgery. Thus, 59 patients have completed initial treatment. Thirty-five of these patients who have completed a minimum of 1 year of follow-up after completion of treatment have been analysed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Recurrence and disease-free survival were assessed clinically by an unblinded investigator who performed personal follow-up, which could introduce bias into outcome assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients were personally followed by one of the authors (A.R.F.). This was done to keep the number of dropouts as few as possible.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no evidence of a pre-registered protocol or statistical analysis plan, and results are reported as an interim analysis on a subset completing 1-year follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This paper presents the first report of an ongoing prospective randomised clinical trial in early T1T2N0 carcinoma of the oral tongue... Thirty-five of these patients who have completed a minimum of 1 year of follow-up after completion of treatment have been analysed.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to substantial attrition and post-randomization exclusions (only 35 of 73 enrolled patients were analyzed), lack of an intention-to-treat approach, and lack of blinding in outcome assessment.
